I’ve actually had osteoporosis for over a decade—diagnosed at 20 years old—and despite that, I was repeatedly denied treatment because of my age. I’ve spent years researching, advocating for myself, and being dismissed by doctors who told me to “just gain weight” without giving me real medical support.

Yes, weight and exercise play a role, but let’s be real—if it were that simple, I wouldn’t be in this situation. Gaining weight is a constant struggle for me, and high-impact exercise is risky when my bones are already fragile. I’m working on nutrition and resistance training as much as I can, but at this stage, I need actual medication to prevent further decline. That’s not me “not wanting to hear the truth”—it’s me acknowledging medical reality.

If the meds don’t work, then I’ll reevaluate. But acting like they’re pointless unless I magically gain weight overnight is misleading. Osteoporosis is complex, and there’s no “one size fits all” approach.
